Claude (Sonnet 4.6) refinement with validator (validate_mentions.py span-overlap/person-id-aware Rule C; added ~28 Rule-C-caught misses on first pass) plus a full manual read-through of the entire ~2-hour transcript (added ~75 further missed mentions the validator's Rule C could not catch on its own, including an entire previously-uncaptured character arc, plus corrected numerous timestamp errors introduced during this pass)
notes: This is one of the longest and most detailed episodes processed (2974 transcript lines, ~2 hours), structured as a business-breakup narrative between Krzysztof Gonciarz and Katarzyna Meciński (243 mentions -- the highest single-figure count across all processed episodes). The most significant finding from the manual read-through: the entire character arc of 'Ewa Nowakowska' (id 25, alias 'menedżerka z Tofu') -- roughly 20 mentions covering a former Tofu Media colleague central to a whole subplot -- was completely absent from the naive draft and only surfaced by reading context around an unrelated fix; this is a good example of why full manual reading remains necessary even after the validator reports clean. Numerous wordplay/nickname coinages for Katarzyna Meciński were found and included after confirming context: 'Kasiański' (a mocking Instagram-handle-style nickname), 'katarzynizm' (mocking neologism), and 'Casi' (a business-name pun, 'Asahi Casi'). Two English-language voicemail clips ('Kha's not responding to my emails') appear twice (opening and again near the end) and were both captured. One false-positive risk was intentionally left unmarked and documented: after 'Bestii z'/'Tokio' (the alias 'Bestia z Tokio') was correctly captured as a multi-line mention, the bare word 'Tokio' also matches five unrelated literal references to the city of Tokyo elsewhere in the transcript (where Krzysztof Gonciarz lived and worked) -- these residual Rule C warnings are expected and not real misses, consistent with similar coincidental-substring patterns in other episodes (e.g. 'Wi' in episode 6, 'mają' in episode 12). Several timestamp errors introduced during the extensive manual-addition process were caught and corrected by repeatedly re-running the validator rather than treating any single pass as final.
